citation: Vaughn, S., Swanson, E., Fall, A.-M., Roberts, G., Capin, P., Stevens, E. A., & Stewart, A. A. (2022). The efficacy of comprehension and vocabulary focused professional development on English learners' literacy. Journal of Educational Psychology, 114(2), 257-272. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000684
report_number: ERIC Grantee Submission ED618777 (IES grantee; STRIVE project, IES R305A150407); journal article EJ1325060
design: Cluster (school)-randomized RCT (STRIVE). Multiple-cohort (3 cohorts, 2016-2019). 81 schools randomized to researcher-supported PD (RPD, n=26), school-supported PD (SPD, n=28), or business-as-usual (BAU, n=27); 2 schools withdrew (1 BAU, 1 RPD) -> 79 analyzed. RPD+SPD pooled into a single STRIVE treatment vs BAU. 235 fourth-grade teachers, 4,757 students (3,594 non-ELs, 921 ELs; some Spanish-version students excluded). Grade 4 only. Subject: content-area (social studies) literacy / reading comprehension & vocabulary. Three-level (student/teacher/school) multilevel models with pretest covariates at all three levels.
problems: ARM MAPPING (documented, not guessed): This single paper reports STRIVE-vs-BAU effects separately for two student populations -- non-ELs and ELs -- and the meta-analysis (Visscher et al. 2025) coded two 'Vaughn et al. 2022' entries differing only on the moderator 'Targeted Population' (row 125 = Specific, row 126 = All). Mapping used: row 125 (Specific) = ELs (the targeted/specific subgroup, Table 6 EL column); row 126 (All) = non-ELs (the broader/non-targeted population, Table 6 non-EL column). The paper does NOT report a single pooled all-students ES in this article; the full-sample main-effect ES live in the companion main-effects paper Capin et al. (2021), which this article references (school-level g 1.30-1.42 content knowledge, 1.19-1.32 vocabulary, .42-.65 content reading comprehension, .05-.10 Gates comprehension, .35-.79 Gates vocabulary). If central merge prefers a true all-students ES for row 126, those Capin 2021 values should be substituted. ICCs recorded are the 3-level school-level (design-effect) ICCs from Table 5 (content measures) and the Level-3 ICCs from Table 7 (Gates). n_clusters recorded as total analyzed schools (79); per-arm school split not given by measure. n_t/n_c are posttest analytic n's by population x condition from Table 4 (STRIVE = pooled RPD+SPD). Gates comprehension n's are reduced (one district capped testing time; analysis used 37 schools for that measure).
